name: pcapmirror
desc: Tool for capturing network traffic on remote host using TZSP or ERSPAN
why: Captures remote traffic mirrored via TZSP or ERSPAN, opening a door into encapsulation protocols few developers touch.

brief.what_it_is: pcapmirror is a command-line tool that captures network traffic with libpcap and sends the captured packets to a remote destination, encapsulated in TZSP. It accepts BPF filter syntax to select which traffic is captured. The page describes it as useful for network monitoring, intrusion detection, and remote packet analysis. The brew description and scout notes also mention ERSPAN, but the project page I read mentions only TZSP.
brief.why_it_exists: The project page describes it as a simple packet mirroring tool for network monitoring, intrusion detection, and remote packet analysis.
brief.how_it_works: It uses the libpcap library to capture packets, applies optional BPF filters, and encapsulates the captured traffic in TZSP for transmission to a remote destination. The README text I could read does not go into further detail.
brief.install_notes: The brew formula names one executable, pcapmirror. The project page gives no build, dependency, or configuration steps, and the README body did not load.
brief.standout: It sends mirrored traffic in TZSP, the encapsulation used by TaZmen Sniffer Protocol, which most developers rarely meet. Pairing that with libpcap BPF filtering makes it a small bridge between packet capture and remote mirror receivers.
brief.status: unknown. The project page shows a creation date of March 20, 2025 and a BSD 3-Clause license. I found no release date, last commit date, or maintenance note. The README file page loaded with no visible content.
brief.caveats: The README body did not render, so I could not check commands, options, or setup steps. The project page mentions only TZSP, while the brew description and scout notes say TZSP or ERSPAN. Treat the ERSPAN support as unconfirmed. The project page also describes the tool as sending traffic to a remote destination, while the brew description says it captures on a remote host. Those are different descriptions and should be checked against the code before the entry claims either one.
quotes: A simple packet mirroring tool using libpcap
pcapmirror is a command-line tool for capturing network traffic and mirroring it to a remote destination using TZSP encapsulation.
It leverages the libpcap library for packet capture and provides options for filtering traffic based on BPF syntax.
